summary: The fix closes the claimed cause: a cost-state line cut at any of 148 byte offsets (mid-UTF-8 included), and a half-written user line that quotes cost-state, both fall back to the previous complete cost-state. A recorded run keeps its cost across the partial reading, a genuine restart is still counted, an unreadable transcript yields no reading rather than a zero, and all 166 core tests pass. Two problems remain. The 4.0.1 CHANGELOG does not mention the jump fix the user asked to release, although 4.0.0 had the same zero-reading path. Separately, a stale prompt baseline still over-credits a run with spending from before it started (pre-existing).

findings.title: 4.0.1 CHANGELOG omits the run-cost jump fix the release was cut for
findings.evidence: CHANGELOG.md:9-31 lists only the in-turn pricing, the #24 reviewer fix, the band and the size cap; nothing about the doubled counter ($857 -> $1714). The same path shipped in v4.0.0: `git show v4.0.0:scripts/cvcore/usage.py` has `_parse` raising on a partial line, so `last_cost_state` returned None and `session_total` returned 0.0 for transcripts <= 8 MB, which triggered the `start_usd -= last_usd` restart branch. 4.0.0 users can hit it, and `release_notes.py 4.0.1` produces notes that do not say it is fixed.
findings.reproduce: grep -n 'half\|restart\|new process\|still being written' CHANGELOG.md | head -3; python3 .github/scripts/release_notes.py 4.0.1 procoders/superpowers-v --out /dev/stdout
findings.recommendation: Add a Fixed bullet: a cost-state line Claude Code was still writing read as 'no turn yet' (cli $0), so the run was credited the whole session again; an unparsable line is now skipped (scripts/cvcore/usage.py `_parse`).

findings.title: Prompt baseline is written once and kept, so a later run is credited spending from before it started
findings.evidence: scripts/cvcore/hooks.py:261-265 `_arm` writes baseline-<sid> only `if not base.exists()`, and the file is removed only in `_attach` (hooks.py:78-79) once a run records usage. A session that had an unbound prompt at $1, then worked to $50 before the prompt that starts a run, gets start_usd = 1.0. The intended semantics (tests/core/test_hooks.py:273 `test_prompt_records_baseline_before_work`) count from the prompt that led to the run. This is pre-existing and not introduced by this diff, but it feeds a wrong baseline into apply_cost and inflates the band the same way the user reported.
findings.reproduce: cd CHECKOUT && python3 .review-probes/p2.py   # prints run_cost 54.0; spending since the run's prompt is 5.0
findings.recommendation: Refresh the baseline on every unbound prompt (drop the `if not base.exists()` guard, keep the unpriced check), so it always holds the cost at the latest prompt before the run is created.
